title: Production Spark -- EMR deployment, Spark UI, Structured Streaming
exp: Reading the Spark UI is the difference between guessing at performance problems and diagnosing them.
pts: Spark UI (port 4040 locally, EMR History Server in prod): Jobs -> Stages -> Tasks. Find slow stage; check task duration outliers and Exchange operators.
EMR step: upload .py to S3, submit with --deploy-mode cluster.
Structured Streaming: read from stream source as a DataFrame; Spark processes micro-batches continuously.
Checkpoint: records stream progress. On restart, resumes exactly where it stopped.
trigger(availableNow=True): process all available data right now and stop.
code:
# STRUCTURED STREAMING
from pyspark.sql.functions import window
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StringType, DoubleType

schema = StructType().add('order_id', StringType()).add('amount', DoubleType())

stream = (spark.readStream
    .format('json')
    .schema(schema)
    .option('path', 's3://bucket/incoming/')
    .load())

processed = (stream
    .filter(col('amount') > 0)
    .withWatermark('timestamp', '10 minutes')
    .groupBy(window('timestamp', '5 minutes'), 'customer_id')
    .agg({'amount': 'sum'}))

query = (processed.writeStream
    .outputMode('append')
    .format('parquet')
    .option('path', 's3://bucket/streaming-output/')
    .option('checkpointLocation', 's3://bucket/checkpoints/orders/')
    .trigger(processingTime='1 minute')
    .start())
query.awaitTermination()

viz.cap: Structured Streaming micro-batch pipeline -- runs continuously

qa.q: What to look for in the Spark UI for a slow job?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Jobs tab: which job is slow. Stages tab: find slow stage. In that stage Tasks tab: median vs max task duration (big gap = skew), input size per task (outlier = skew). DAG Visualization: Exchange nodes (shuffles). A healthy stage has all tasks completing within 2-3x of each other.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Async methods compile into an IAsyncStateMachine struct managed by the AsyncMethodBuilder. Awaiting an uncompleted task yields execution back to the caller. Blocking with .Result on a thread bound to a SynchronizationContext causes deadlocks when the continuation waits for the blocked thread.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) on ASP.NET request threads rapidly exhausts thread pool threads, leading to HTTP 503 gateway timeouts and request queuing under load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async all the way preserves thread pool scalability, but requires passing CancellationToken through all layers and avoiding sync blocking methods everywhere.

qa.q: Why is checkpointing mandatory in Structured Streaming?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The checkpoint directory records the stream offset (how far the job has processed) and aggregation state. On crash and restart, Spark reads the checkpoint and resumes exactly where it stopped -- not reprocessing everything. Without checkpointing, a restart reprocesses all data or loses progress.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.
